Study full-channel paired maps through overlapping coefficient windows (#215)

## Result and scope

This PR adds `AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001`, a written, unreviewed
obstruction for paired-source maps with fixed injective
polynomial-column routing and arbitrary regular square channel matrices.
The first map and auxiliary maps may have Laurent poles, and the two
tensor contributions may cancel poles.

For target first dimension `D = lr`, covered-coordinate count `N`,
good-leading-coordinate count `G`, and overlap-component product `c`,
the auxiliary first-flattening rank is at least `max(0, D - N + G - c)`.
The formal flattening statement holds over every field; over C it also
bounds ordinary border rank. At fixed width and near-full outer
dimensions, only `o(n)` singular leading channel blocks force `n^2 -
o(n^2)` repair cost. Full channel rank is allowed.

The proof accounts separately for the ordinary leading intersection, all
new directions created by saturation, and cancellation through the
saturated auxiliary-kernel lattice. General column-mixing maps and
extensively singular leading families remain outside this obstruction.
No improved exponent is claimed.

## Evidence and dependencies

- Add the proof, source pins, standard-library exact rational verifier,
retained seven-case control report, and six package tests.
- Reconstruct native source terms and independently reconstruct
coefficient-window slices. Controls cover separated integer
restrictions, a full-channel example attaining the `D - 1`
first-flattening bound, boundary windows, actual leading rank loss,
polar cancellation, and a moving restriction that requires the
saturation correction.
- Register one new claim and update status, active-work, and provenance
summaries. Preserve all 295 existing main claim objects, existing
source/code/dependency/workflow files, and both protected research
archives.
- Both runtime source pins are on `bd03b9d`. PR211 is credited at
immutable head `1cce4e64`; its proof digest verifies, it is not a
runtime dependency, and the necessary saturated-kernel argument is
reproduced here without its earlier low-channel-rank hypothesis.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `f8fdcd314d7a0740ebc36e70e76b348b8fa33935`; exact tree:
`bd8908108844b3ea4e212204bbed15d54668d89a`.

All 27 executed tests passed: six package tests, nine repository
metadata/archive checks, and 12 baseline profile/support checks. The
retained report matches all seven native controls, covering 4,277 target
coefficient positions and 23,722 source-slice positions. The damaged
integer construction is rejected. No full regression or historical
replay was rerun for this focused review.

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_column_overlap.py -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research.py -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_archive_integrity.py -v
```

Required hosted CI must pass on the final mergeable head. This review
does not change the claim's written-unreviewed status or constitute
independent mathematical review.



## Current-main integration — 2026-10-23

Commit `9b0bb20a6a891d9d352029d7775d650e065a51ea` incorporates main
`9bcee612569b9f56c8a48ed91a5ebd7ebfaef3b2` after #217 merged. The
integrated tree is `e23c60d866f32b350c211ee74de1a959f11d8038`. All 297
combined claim records retain their exact objects and raw record bytes;
the source packages, proofs, certificates, archives, and historical
validation receipts are unchanged. Shared summaries retain both
contributions.

All 10 focused repository, archive, source-pin, and claim-scope checks
passed on this integration. The earlier review and regression evidence
above remains tied to its stated revisions. Required hosted CI must pass
on this new head before merge.

+# Full-channel overlap and the cost of leading rank loss
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed OpenAI Codex work. Claim
+`AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001` is written and unreviewed.
+No matrix multiplication exponent improves.
+
+## 1. Result and scope
+
+The paired source is
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}=\sum_{p,q<n}\sum_{y,v<m}
+ A_{p,q}B_{y,q+v}C_{p+y,v},\qquad n\ge1,\quad m\ge2.
+\]
+
+Its first leg has dimension `n^2`; each other leg has dimension
+`m(n+m-1)`. The target is
+
+\[
+M(l,m,r)=\sum_{i<l,j<r,\alpha<m}
+ a_{i,j}b_{j,\alpha}c_{\alpha,i},\qquad D=lr.
+\]
+
+Work over a field K, with O=K[[t]] and L=K((t)). Choose injections
+
+\[
+\sigma_B:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\},
+\quad
+\sigma_C:\{0,\ldots,l-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\}.
+\]
+
+At retained source polynomial columns, the long maps are
+
+\[
+B_{y,\sigma_B(j)}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\alpha<m}\beta_j(t)_{y,\alpha}b_{j,\alpha},\qquad
+C_{\sigma_C(i),v}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\delta<m}\gamma_i(t)_{v,\delta}c_{\delta,i},       \tag{1}
+\]
+
+where each channel matrix belongs to Mat_m(O). Other source columns
+map to zero. The coefficients may depend arbitrarily on the retained
+column. In particular, their common shift-window span and their channel
+rank may both be full. The routing injections are fixed for the family.
+
+For a source column s define its covered first indices
+
+\[
+J(s)=\{s-m+1,\ldots,s\}\cap\{0,\ldots,n-1\}.
+\]
+
+Let U_B be the union of J(sigma_B(j)) over all retained B columns.
+Let U_B^g use only columns whose beta_j(0) is invertible. Define U_C and
+U_C^g in the same way. Put
+
+\[
+N=|U_B||U_C|,\qquad G=|U_B^g||U_C^g|.
+\]
+
+For each side, retain only its good source-column positions in the full
+window interval `[m-1,n-1]`. Join two positions when their distance is
+strictly less than m. Let c_B,c_C be the numbers of connected components,
+with zero for an empty set, and put c=c_B c_C.
+
+**Theorem.** Suppose arbitrary Laurent first maps and arbitrary Laurent
+maps on a fixed auxiliary tensor R give
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q_{n,m}+E_R(t)=M(l,m,r)+O(t).            \tag{2}
+\]
+
+The two contributions in (2) need not be regular separately. Then
+
+\[
+\boxed{\operatorname{rank} R_{A\mid BC},\ \underline R(R)
+ \ \ge\ \max(0,D-N+G-c).}                            \tag{3}
+\]
+
+The flattening statement holds over every field for the stated formal
+identity. Over C it gives the displayed usual border-rank lower bound.
+This is a restriction on the maps (1), not a lower bound for arbitrary
+paired-source constructions. Mixing distinct polynomial columns on
+either long leg is outside the theorem.
+
+## 2. The ordinary leading intersection
+
+Let H_0 be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(0),C(0))Q`. Write a first
+parameter as f=(f_pq), extending it by zero outside the source square.
+At target outer position (i,j), its m-by-m channel block is
+
+\[
+\beta_j(0)^T F_{ij}(f)\gamma_i(0),\qquad
+F_{ij}(f)_{y,v}=f_{\sigma_C(i)-y,\sigma_B(j)-v}.       \tag{4}
+\]
+
+Let T be the target first-slice plane. Its blocks are `w_ij I_m`.
+If either channel matrix in (4) is singular, equality with a target
+slice forces w_ij=0. The same conclusion holds if either window is
+outside `[m-1,n-1]`: F then has a zero row or a zero column.
+
+At a remaining good pair, both matrices are invertible, so
+
+\[
+F_{ij}(f)=w_{ij}\,\beta_j(0)^{-T}\gamma_i(0)^{-1}.
+                                                               \tag{5}
+\]
+
+Consider two good C positions separated by delta with `0<delta<m`,
+and fix one good B position. Their windows share `m-delta` full rows.
+Restricting (5) to these common source rows gives
+
+\[
+w_{ij}K=w_{i'j}K',                                      \tag{6}
+\]
+
+where K and K' are nonzero matrices. Each consists of a nonempty subset
+of rows of an invertible matrix. Thus the two scalar coordinates either
+are proportional with a fixed nonzero ratio, or both must vanish.
+The same argument for B positions uses common columns.
+
+The graph on good outer pairs is the Cartesian product of the two
+position graphs. It has c_B c_C connected components. Along each
+component, (6) leaves at most one scalar degree of freedom; a cycle may
+remove that degree of freedom. All other scalar coordinates vanish.
+Consequently
+
+\[
+\dim(H_0\cap T)\le c.                                 \tag{7}
+\]
+
+This argument needs invertibility of individual channel matrices, not
+low rank of a common channel factor. It also explains why separated
+routing components cannot be omitted from the bound.
+
+## 3. Count every direction created by a singular leading map
+
+Let H(t) be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(t),C(t))Q` over L, and
+write r_gen=dim H(t), r_0=dim H_0. Source parameters outside U_C x U_B
+have zero image for every t, hence
+
+\[
+r_{\rm gen}\le N.                                     \tag{8}
+\]
+
+At every good leading pair, (4) can be inverted to read the entire
+coefficient window of f. These windows cover U_C^g x U_B^g. A parameter
+in the leading slice-map kernel therefore vanishes on every one of its
+G coordinates, proving
+
+\[
+r_0\ge G.                                              \tag{9}
+\]
+
+Let bar(H) be the saturated limit of H(t): intersect H(t) with the
+ambient free O-module and reduce modulo t. This intersection is a
+saturated submodule over the discrete valuation ring O. A Smith basis,
+or successive elimination of lowest valuations, shows that its reduction
+has dimension r_gen. Every regular source column reduces into bar(H),
+so H_0 is contained in bar(H). Therefore
+
+\[
+\dim\bigl(\bar H/H_0\bigr)=r_{\rm gen}-r_0\le N-G.
+\]
+
+Passing from H_0 to bar(H) can enlarge its intersection with any fixed
+linear space by at most that quotient dimension. Combining with (7),
+
+\[
+\dim(\bar H\cap T)\le c+N-G.                          \tag{10}
+\]
+
+In particular, no coefficientwise limit of a raw polar source column
+has been taken. Saturation accounts for cancellations and for every
+new slice direction.
+
+## 4. Auxiliary poles cannot evade the dimension budget
+
+Let k be the first flattening rank of E_R(t) over L. It is at most the
+first flattening rank of R. Its kernel V in the D-dimensional target
+first-covector space has dimension at least D-k.
+
+The saturated lattice V intersect O^D has a reduction bar(V) of the same
+dimension. For each of its basis vectors w(t), equation (2) gives
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q(w(t))
+ =M(w(0))+O(t),                                        \tag{11}
+\]
+
+because E_R(t)(w(t)) is exactly zero over L. Each right side lies in the
+saturated source lattice. Its reduction lies in bar(H). Since M has
+injective first flattening, the independent vectors of bar(V) give at
+least D-k independent members of bar(H) intersect T. By (10),
+
+\[
+D-k\le c+N-G.
+\]
+
+This proves the flattening bound (3). A tensor of border rank q has
+first flattening rank at most q: its `(q+1)` minors vanish on rank-q
+tensors and on their closure. This supplies the border-rank conclusion.
+Ramified formal parameters may be renamed t. No bound on first-map or
+auxiliary pole orders is needed.
+
+## 5. Consequences for a scalable construction
+
+If every retained leading channel matrix is invertible, U_B^g=U_B and
+U_C^g=U_C. The lower bound is simply
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge D-c_Bc_C.                          \tag{12}
+\]
+
+For contiguous full-window routing on each side, c_B=c_C=1. Thus even
+full channel rank leaves an auxiliary first-flattening cost at least
+`lr-1`. Arbitrary first-map poles do not change this conclusion.
+
+More generally, fix m and take l/n,r/n to one. Suppose all but o(n) of
+the retained leading channel matrices are invertible on each side.
+The retained injections omit o(n) source columns. A good source-column
+set of size n-o(n) covers n-o(n) first indices: the map
+`s -> min(s,n-1)` is injective except for at most m-1 upper-end positions.
+Thus G=n^2-o(n^2), while N is at most n^2.
+
+Each extra connected component among the good interior positions needs
+at least m-1 missing positions between components. Hence c_B,c_C=o(n),
+and (3) yields
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge n^2-o(n^2).                        \tag{13}
+\]
+
+The construction criterion requires a subquadratic correction. A route
+within (1) must therefore use extensive leading singularity, or change
+the routing model to mix polynomial columns.
+
+There is a quantitative version, still with fixed m and l/n,r/n tending
+to one. Suppose the fractions of retained
+leading invertible blocks, divided by n, tend to alpha and beta. The
+coverage and missing-position counts above imply
+
+\[
+\liminf\frac{\underline R(R)}{n^2}
+ \ge \max\left(0,\alpha\beta-
+  \frac{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}{(m-1)^2}\right).           \tag{14}
+\]
+
+For equal fractions alpha=beta, a subquadratic correction requires
+`alpha<=1/m`. At width four, retaining a nonsingular leading channel
+block on more than one quarter of each long leg already forces a
+positive quadratic cost by this estimate. This is a necessary condition
+inside (1), not a claim that the remaining singular families work.
+
+## 6. Exact constructions that test the boundary
+
+### Separated windows give a genuine restriction
+
+Put k=floor(n/m), and select source polynomial positions
+`s_i=m(i+1)-1`, for i<k, on both long legs. Use identity channel maps.
+The windows are disjoint. Map a source A coordinate to a_ij exactly
+when
+
+\[
+p=mi+m-1-y,\quad q=mj+m-1-y
+\quad\text{for some }0\le y<m,
+\]
+
+and to zero otherwise. Literal substitution gives
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}\ \ge\ M(k,m,k)                                \tag{15}
+\]
+
+over every field, with unit coefficients and no cancellation. Here
+c_Bc_C=k^2=D and (12) permits zero repair. The outer ratio is about 1/m,
+so this calibration does not supply the near-full construction criterion.
+

+"""Exact native-source controls for the full-channel overlap theorem.
+
+Only the Python standard library is used. Complete tensor coefficients,
+including all implicit zeros, are compared. Formal maps are finite Laurent
+polynomials over Q; no floating-point decision is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def rank(rows):
+    """Rank of sparse rational rows without modifying the input."""
+    pivots = {}
+    for raw in rows:
+        row = {k: F(v) for k, v in raw.items() if v}
+        while row:
+            p = min(row)
+            if p not in pivots:
+                scale = row[p]
+                pivots[p] = {k: v / scale for k, v in row.items()}
+                break
+            scale = row[p]
+            for k, v in pivots[p].items():
+                value = row.get(k, F(0)) - scale * v
+                if value:
+                    row[k] = value
+                else:
+                    row.pop(k, None)
+    return len(pivots)
+
+
+def dense_rank(matrix):
+    return rank([{j: value for j, value in enumerate(row) if value}
+                 for row in matrix])
+
+
+def inverse(matrix):
+    n = len(matrix)
+    rows = [[F(v) for v in row] + [F(i == j) for j in range(n)]
+            for i, row in enumerate(matrix)]
+    for j in range(n):
+        p = next(i for i in range(j, n) if rows[i][j])
+        rows[p], rows[j] = rows[j], rows[p]
+        scale = rows[j][j]
+        rows[j] = [value / scale for value in rows[j]]
+        for i in range(n):
+            if i != j and rows[i][j]:
+                scale = rows[i][j]
+                rows[i] = [a - scale * b for a, b in zip(rows[i], rows[j])]
+    return [row[n:] for row in rows]
+
+
+def identity(m):
+    return [[F(i == j) for j in range(m)] for i in range(m)]
+
+
+def poly(value=0, degree=0):
+    return {degree: F(value)} if value else {}
+
+
+def add(left, right, scale=1):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for degree, value in right.items():
+        new = out.get(degree, F(0)) + scale * value
+        if new:
+            out[degree] = new
+        else:
+            out.pop(degree, None)
+    return out
+
+
+def mul(left, right):
+    out = {}
+    for a, x in left.items():
+        for b, y in right.items():
+            out = add(out, {a + b: x * y})
+    return out
+
+
+def evaluate(value, t):
+    return sum((coefficient * F(t) ** degree
+                for degree, coefficient in value.items()), F(0))
+
+
+def constant_blocks(matrices):
+    return [[[poly(value) for value in row] for row in matrix]
+            for matrix in matrices]
+
+
+def constant_first(values):
+    return {pq: {a: poly(value) for a, value in images.items() if value}
+            for pq, images in values.items()}
+
+
+def target(l, m, r):
+    return {(i * r + j, j * m + a, a * l + i): poly(1)
+            for i, j, a in itertools.product(range(l), range(r), range(m))}
+
+
+def native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first):
+    """Expand the literal n^2*m^2 source terms and all local-map entries."""
+    b_index, c_index = {s: j for j, s in enumerate(sb)}, {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sc)}
+    l = len(sc)
+    out = {}
+    expanded = 0
+    for p, q, y, v in itertools.product(range(n), range(n), range(m), range(m)):
+        j, i = b_index.get(q + v), c_index.get(p + y)
+        if j is None or i is None:
+            continue
+        for a, av in first.get((p, q), {}).items():
+            for alpha, bv in enumerate(beta[j][y]):
+                if not bv:
+                    continue
+                for delta, cv in enumerate(gamma[i][v]):
+                    if not cv:
+                        continue
+                    term = mul(mul(av, bv), cv)
+                    key = (a, j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                    out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), term)
+                    expanded += 1
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}, expanded
+
+
+def window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, at=0):
+    """Reconstruct source slices from coefficient windows, independently of native()."""
+    l = len(sc)
+    bs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in beta]
+    cs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in gamma]
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(n * n)]
+    for i, z in enumerate(sc):
+        for j, s in enumerate(sb):
+            for y in range(m):
+                for v in range(m):
+                    p, q = z - y, s - v
+                    if not (0 <= p < n and 0 <= q < n):
+                        continue
+                    row = rows[p * n + q]
+                    for alpha in range(m):
+                        for delta in range(m):
+                            value = bs[j][y][alpha] * cs[i][v][delta]
+                            if value:
+                                key = (j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                                row[key] = row.get(key, F(0)) + value
+    return [{key: value for key, value in row.items() if value} for row in rows]
+
+
+def target_rows(l, m, r):
+    return [{(j * m + a, a * l + i): F(1) for a in range(m)}
+            for i in range(l) for j in range(r)]
+
+
+def covered(n, m, positions):
+    return sorted({q for s in positions for q in range(max(0, s - m + 1), min(n, s + 1))})
+
+
+def components(n, m, positions):
+    values = sorted(s for s in positions if m - 1 <= s <= n - 1)
+    groups = []
+    for value in values:
+        if not groups or value - groups[-1][-1] >= m:
+            groups.append([])
+        groups[-1].append(value)
+    return groups
+
+
+def geometry(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma):
+    good = []
+    for positions, blocks in ((sb, beta), (sc, gamma)):
+        good.append([s for s, block in zip(positions, blocks)
+                     if dense_rank([[evaluate(value, 0) for value in row]
+                                    for row in block]) == m])
+    ub, uc = covered(n, m, sb), covered(n, m, sc)
+    gb, gc = covered(n, m, good[0]), covered(n, m, good[1])
+    cb, cc = components(n, m, good[0]), components(n, m, good[1])
+    d, nn, gg, c = len(sb) * len(sc), len(ub) * len(uc), len(gb) * len(gc), len(cb) * len(cc)
+    return {"all_covered": [ub, uc], "good_covered": [gb, gc],
+            "good_source_columns": good, "components": [cb, cc],
+            "D": d, "N": nn, "G": gg, "c": c,
+            "auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound": max(0, d - nn + gg - c)}
+
+
+def subtract_tensor(left, right):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for key, value in right.items():
+        out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), value, -1)
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}
+
+
+def tensor_rows(tensor, count, at):
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(count)]
+    for (a, b, c), value in tensor.items():
+        coefficient = evaluate(value, at)
+        if coefficient:
+            rows[a][(b, c)] = coefficient
+    return rows
+
+
+def serial_tensor(tensor):
+    return [[*key, [[degree, str(value)] for degree, value in sorted(poly_value.items())]]
+            for key, poly_value in sorted(tensor.items())]
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def inspect_case(name, n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first, expected_exact=False,
+                 expected_residual_rank=None, require_poles=False):
+    if n < 1 or m < 2 or len(set(sb)) != len(sb) or len(set(sc)) != len(sc):
+        raise ValueError("Positive source sizes and injective routing are required")
+    if any(s < 0 or s >= n + m - 1 for s in sb + sc):
+        raise ValueError("Source routing column is outside the polynomial range")
+    l, r, d = len(sc), len(sb), len(sc) * len(sb)
+    source_tensor, expanded = native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first)
+    wanted = target(l, m, r)
+    residual = subtract_tensor(wanted, source_tensor)
+    if expected_exact and residual:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "constructed target identity failed"))
+    # Literal coefficientwise cancellation, including every negative order.
+    if residual and subtract_tensor(wanted, subtract_tensor(source_tensor, residual)) == {}:
+        raise AssertionError("The deliberately wrong residual sign passed")
+    total = subtract_tensor(source_tensor, {key: {e: -v for e, v in value.items()}
+                                           for key, value in residual.items()})
+    if total != wanted:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "complete cancellation identity failed"))
+    negative = sum(1 for value in source_tensor.values() for e in value if e < 0)
+    if require_poles and not negative:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "missing negative source coefficients"))
+    data = geometry(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma)
+    h0 = window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma)
+    h2 = window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, 2)
+    r0, r2 = rank(h0), rank(h2)
+    intersection = r0 + d - rank(h0 + target_rows(l, m, r))
+    if not (r0 >= data["G"] and r2 <= data["N"] and intersection <= data["c"]):
+        raise AssertionError((name, "dimension estimate failed", data, r0, r2, intersection))
+    native_first = constant_first({(p, q): {p * n + q: 1} for p in range(n) for q in range(n)})
+    full, _ = native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, native_first)
+    for at, reconstructed in ((0, h0), (2, h2)):
+        if tensor_rows(full, n * n, at) != reconstructed:
+            raise AssertionError((name, "native/window reconstruction disagrees", at))
+    rr = rank(tensor_rows(residual, d, 2))
+    # Evaluation supplies a certified minor over Q(t). If this is D, the
+    # rank is exactly D. Constant controls have their exact ordinary rank.
+    if rr < data["auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound"]:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "observed exact control violates the bound"))
+    if expected_residual_rank is not None and rr != expected_residual_rank:
+        raise AssertionError((name, rr, expected_residual_rank))
+    channel = [[F(0) for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(m)]
+    for (a, b, c_index), value in source_tensor.items():
+        if a == 0:
+            j, alpha = divmod(b, m)
+            delta, i = divmod(c_index, l)
+            channel[alpha][delta] += evaluate(value, 2) * F(2) ** j * F(3) ** i
+    channel_rank = dense_rank(channel)
+    return {"name": name, "n": n, "m": m, "target_shape": [l, m, r],
+            "routing_B": sb, "routing_C": sc, "geometry": data,
+            "leading_source_rank": r0, "source_rank_at_t2": r2,
+            "leading_target_intersection_dimension": intersection,
+            "residual_rank_at_t2": rr,
+            "residual_rank_is_exact_over_Qt": rr == d or not require_poles,
+            "source_terms": n * n * m * m,
+            "expanded_native_terms": expanded,
+            "target_coefficient_positions": m * m * d * d,
+            "source_slice_coefficient_positions_per_evaluation": n * n * m * m * d,
+            "source_negative_coefficients": negative,
+            "source_A0_channel_rank_at_t2_X2_Y3": channel_rank,
+            "complete_source_sha256": digest(serial_tensor(source_tensor)),
+            "complete_residual_sha256": digest(serial_tensor(residual)),
+            "exact_target": not residual}
+
+
+def separated_case(n, m):
+    k = n // m
+    positions = [m * (i + 1) - 1 for i in range(k)]
+    first = {(m * i + m - 1 - y, m * j + m - 1 - y): {i * k + j: 1}
+             for i, j, y in itertools.product(range(k), range(k), range(m))}
+    blocks = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    return inspect_case(f"separated-n{n}-m{m}", n, m, positions, positions,
+                        blocks, blocks, constant_first(first), expected_exact=True,
+                        expected_residual_rank=0)
+
+
+def vandermonde_case(n=5, m=3):
+    positions = list(range(m - 1, n))
+    lam = list(range(1, m + 1))
+    vi = inverse([[F(a) ** (-y) for a in lam] for y in range(m)])
+    beta, gamma = [], []
+    for s in positions:
+        beta.append([[vi[a][y] * F(lam[a]) ** (-s) for a in range(m)]
+                     for y in range(m)])
+        gamma.append([[vi[a][v] * F(lam[a]) ** (-s) for a in range(m)]
+                      for v in range(m)])
+    first = {(p, q): {0: sum(F(a) ** (p + q) for a in lam)}
+             for p in range(n) for q in range(n)}
+    result = inspect_case("connected-full-channel-sharp", n, m, positions, positions,
+                          constant_blocks(beta), constant_blocks(gamma),
+                          constant_first(first), expected_residual_rank=len(positions) ** 2 - 1)
+    if result["leading_target_intersection_dimension"] != 1:
+        raise AssertionError("Sharp example has the wrong intersection dimension")
+    if result["source_A0_channel_rank_at_t2_X2_Y3"] != m:
+        raise AssertionError("The full-channel control lost channel rank")
+    return result
+
+
+def moving_separated_case():
+    n, m, k = 6, 2, 3
+    positions = [1, 3, 5]
+    beta = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    gamma = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    beta[1] = [[poly(i == j, 1) for j in range(m)] for i in range(m)]
+    first = {(m * i + m - 1 - y, m * j + m - 1 - y):
+             {i * k + j: poly(1, -int(j == 1))}
+             for i, j, y in itertools.product(range(k), range(k), range(m))}
+    result = inspect_case("exact-moving-target-requires-saturation-budget", n, m,
+                          positions, positions, beta, gamma, first,
+                          expected_exact=True, expected_residual_rank=0)
+    if result["geometry"]["D"] - result["geometry"]["c"] <= 0:
+        raise AssertionError("The omitted-saturation counterexample is ineffective")
+    return result
+
+
+def varying_case():
+    n, m = 5, 2
+    positions = [1, 2, 3, 4]
+    blocks_b = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    blocks_c = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    blocks_b[1][1][1] = poly(1, 1)
+    first = {(p, q): {0: poly(1 + p + 2 * q, -1)}
+             for p in range(n) for q in range(n)}
+    return inspect_case("singular-leading-block-with-pole-cancellation", n, m,
+                        positions, positions, blocks_b, blocks_c, first,
+                        require_poles=True, expected_residual_rank=16)
+
+
+def boundary_case():
+    n, m = 3, 3
+    positions_b, positions_c = [0, 1, 3, 4], [0, 2, 4]
+    first = {(p, q): {(p + 2 * q) % 12: 1 + p + q} for p in range(n) for q in range(n)}
+    return inspect_case("zero-extension-boundary-columns", n, m, positions_b, positions_c,
+                        constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions_b]),
+                        constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions_c]),
+                        constant_first(first), expected_residual_rank=12)
+
+
+def leading_loss_case():
+    n, m = 4, 2
+    positions = [1, 2, 3]
+    beta = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    gamma = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    for j in (0, 1):
+        beta[j][0][0] = poly(1, 1)
+        beta[j][1][1] = poly(1, 1)
+    first = {(p, q): {0: poly(1 + p + q, -1)}
+             for p in range(n) for q in range(n)}
+    result = inspect_case("actual-leading-slice-rank-loss", n, m, positions, positions,
+                          beta, gamma, first, require_poles=True, expected_residual_rank=9)
+    if result["source_rank_at_t2"] <= result["leading_source_rank"]:
+        raise AssertionError("Rank-loss control did not lose rank")
+    return result
+
+
+def run():
+    cases = [separated_case(6, 2), separated_case(8, 4), vandermonde_case(),
+             varying_case(), boundary_case(), leading_loss_case(), moving_separated_case()]
+    return {"schema": "paired-column-overlap-controls-v1", "arithmetic": "exact rational Laurent polynomials",
+            "proof_status": "written-unreviewed", "cases": cases,
+            "case_count": len(cases),
+            "complete_target_positions": sum(c["target_coefficient_positions"] for c in cases),
+            "complete_source_slice_positions": 2 * sum(c["source_slice_coefficient_positions_per_evaluation"] for c in cases),
+            "scope": "Finite controls support proof.md; they do not establish the uniform theorem by extrapolation.",
+            "improves_omega": False}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run()
+    rendered = json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
+    if args.output:
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(rendered)
+    else:
+        print(rendered, end="")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+PACKAGE = ROOT / "research/ai/2026-10-23-column-overlap"
+SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("column_overlap", PACKAGE / "verify.py")
+VERIFY = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
+SPEC.loader.exec_module(VERIFY)
+
+
+class ColumnOverlapTests(unittest.TestCase):

+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.report = VERIFY.run()
+        cls.cases = {value["name"]: value for value in cls.report["cases"]}
+
+    def test_complete_native_replay_matches_retained_report(self):
+        saved = json.loads((ROOT / "results/column-overlap-2026-10-23/controls.json").read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(self.report, saved)
+        self.assertEqual(self.report["case_count"], 7)
+

+    def test_boundary_rank_loss_and_separately_polar_control(self):

+    def test_damaged_integer_construction_is_rejected(self):

+
+    def test_source_pins_and_written_claim_scope(self):
+        sources = json.loads((PACKAGE / "sources.json").read_text())

+        claims = json.loads((ROOT / "research/claims.json").read_text())["claims"]

pulls.body:
## Result and scope

This PR adds `AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001`, a written, unreviewed obstruction for paired-source maps with fixed injective polynomial-column routing and arbitrary regular square channel matrices. The first map and auxiliary maps may have Laurent poles, and the two tensor contributions may cancel poles.

For target first dimension `D = lr`, covered-coordinate count `N`, good-leading-coordinate count `G`, and overlap-component product `c`, the auxiliary first-flattening rank is at least `max(0, D - N + G - c)`. The formal flattening statement holds over every field; over C it also bounds ordinary border rank. At fixed width and near-full outer dimensions, only `o(n)` singular leading channel blocks force `n^2 - o(n^2)` repair cost. Full channel rank is allowed.

The proof accounts separately for the ordinary leading intersection, all new directions created by saturation, and cancellation through the saturated auxiliary-kernel lattice. General column-mixing maps and extensively singular leading families remain outside this obstruction. No improved exponent is claimed.

## Evidence and dependencies

- Add the proof, source pins, standard-library exact rational verifier, retained seven-case control report, and six package tests.
- Reconstruct native source terms and independently reconstruct coefficient-window slices. Controls cover separated integer restrictions, a full-channel example attaining the `D - 1` first-flattening bound, boundary windows, actual leading rank loss, polar cancellation, and a moving restriction that requires the saturation correction.
- Register one new claim and update status, active-work, and provenance summaries. Preserve all 295 existing main claim objects, existing source/code/dependency/workflow files, and both protected research archives.
- Both runtime source pins are on `bd03b9d`. PR211 is credited at immutable head `1cce4e64`; its proof digest verifies, it is not a runtime dependency, and the necessary saturated-kernel argument is reproduced here without its earlier low-channel-rank hypothesis.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `f8fdcd314d7a0740ebc36e70e76b348b8fa33935`; exact tree: `bd8908108844b3ea4e212204bbed15d54668d89a`.

All 27 executed tests passed: six package tests, nine repository metadata/archive checks, and 12 baseline profile/support checks. The retained report matches all seven native controls, covering 4,277 target coefficient positions and 23,722 source-slice positions. The damaged integer construction is rejected. No full regression or historical replay was rerun for this focused review.

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_column_overlap.py -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research.py -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_archive_integrity.py -v
```

Required hosted CI must pass on the final mergeable head. This review does not change the claim's written-unreviewed status or constitute independent mathematical review.



## Current-main integration — 2026-10-23

Commit `9b0bb20a6a891d9d352029d7775d650e065a51ea` incorporates main `9bcee612569b9f56c8a48ed91a5ebd7ebfaef3b2` after #217 merged. The integrated tree is `e23c60d866f32b350c211ee74de1a959f11d8038`. Shared summaries retain both contributions.
